home.faq_a1: FIRST (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) is an international organization that runs robotics competitions for children and teens worldwide.
home.faq_a2: Yes, all core courses, lessons and materials are completely free. Our goal is to make education accessible.
home.faq_a3: FLL Challenge is for ages 9-16, FTC is for ages 12-18, and FGC is for ages 14-18.
home.faq_a4: Theory lessons can be completed without a robot. For hands-on tasks you'll need a LEGO SPIKE Prime (FLL) or goBILDA (FTC) kit.
home.faq_a5: The platform is available in Kazakh, Russian and English. The primary language is Kazakh.
home.faq_q6: How do I create a team?
home.faq_a6: The platform has team-building guides. An FLL team has 2-10 members, FTC teams can have up to 15 members.
home.about_body: Tagylym is an open online platform giving students and mentors from all regions of Kazakhstan free access to structured courses in robotics, programming and engineering. All tracks are built on FIRST values and criteria, not just to teach robot building, but to help teams grow into strong participants, mentors, and future engineers.
home.about_quote: Hundreds of schools with robotics equipment don't use it to its full potential due to lack of content and mentors.
home.problem_body: Today, access to quality STEM education and robotics depends heavily on city, school, and family income: major centers have specialized Lyceums and clubs, while rural schools, even when they have robotics classrooms, often lack content, methodologies, and mentors.
home.problem_quote: Over 60% of Kazakhstan's students study in rural schools and small towns where access to sustainable STEM programs is limited.
